Subscribers are now the slower gate: 381 of 1,000, +8 in 6 days (1.3 a day). Feb needs about 5 a day.

Biggest loss: 3 of 9 long-forms didn't ship. Two were our best topics: hair loss, which had our 1,016-view Short ready to feed it, and stopping tirzepatide.

bottleneck:
Long-form reach still limits watch hours, and subscriber conversion is now the slower gate.
(1) Subscribers: +8 in 6 days (1.3 a day). At that rate it takes about 15 months to get the 619 we still need. Per-video data shows about 3 subs per 1,000 long-form views and about 0.5 per 1,000 Shorts views. Our biggest Short ever (hair grow-back, 1,016 views) logged no subscribers we can see.
(2) Long-form production losses: 3 of 9 long-forms from 10-27 to 11-01 didn't ship, and they were the highest-value topics. "Stop Tirzepatide" was dropped because the narration lost numbers. Retatrutide vs semaglutide was dropped because the voice said "rheumatoid" instead of retatrutide. Hair Loss failed on a fact-check REVISE even though the reviewer called the science solid. The hair one hurts most: it was meant to catch viewers from the 1,016-view Short.
(3) No path from Shorts to long-form: SHORTS and END_SCREEN traffic is 0 on all 20 long-forms with traffic data. Suggested videos bring 68% of practical tirzepatide watch minutes, at 5–6 min per view, and playlist views run 8–12 min. End screens, playlist chains and the Shorts related-video link are still unset.
(4) Packaging on our two most-shown videos: What to Eat (1,290 impressions, 2.79% CTR) and Strength (1,155, 2.68%) click well below our state-change thumbnails (3.8–5.0%).
Newer practical videos also start slowly: Plateau had 87 impressions at day 5 and Bones & Muscle 67 at day 4. Their retention is high (68–79%), so judge them at day 7–28 before reading anything into it.
playbook_markdown:
# InforMed growth playbook: week of 2026-11-03

**Status: off track, but moving.** 95 of 4,000 watch hours. We now earn about 9 h a day (2.7 last week); Feb YPP needs about 33. Subscribers: 381 of 1,000, at +1.3 a day; Feb needs about 5 a day. Lane A (practical tirzepatide) won Exp A: mature videos earn about 340 min each vs 38 for other long-forms. **Every 14:00 long-form this week is Lane A.**

## Long-form (14:00 ET, 8–12 min, label `lane: A`)
1. Ship in this order:
   - "Tirzepatide Hair Loss: Will It Grow Back?" This redoes L1 10-30. Use the hair-loss figures and wording from the craft notes word for word.
   - "What Happens When You Stop Tirzepatide?" This redoes L1 10-27. Use SURMOUNT-4 and include "don't switch, stop or change your medicines on your own".
   - "Tirzepatide and Birth Control Pills: What to Know". Report what the label says only; no instructions. Send viewers to their prescriber.
   - "Why Am I So Tired on Tirzepatide?" Use the label's fatigue rates (5–7% vs 3% on placebo). Cover hydration, protein and sleep, plus when to call the prescriber.
   - "Tirzepatide Injection Site Reactions: What's Normal"
   - "Tirzepatide and Dehydration: Signs and What Helps". Use the label's kidney warning.
2. Each video answers one question that no live Lane A video already answers. Live Lane A videos: What to Eat, Side Effects, Strength, How Long, Plateau, Bones & Muscle, Protein, Thanksgiving, Food Noise, Constipation.
3. Fresh randomized results go to a 13:00 Short. The only news that can get a long-form is a randomized head-to-head against tirzepatide or semaglutide, made public within the last 48 h. It runs as an extra L2 and never replaces Lane A.
4. Still banned in long-form:
   - cost, coverage, Medicare, pharmacy and gray-market topics
   - "What is [drug]?" explainers
   - single-trial deep dives
   - timeline-only topics
   - broad head-term titles

## Packaging
- **Title:** the question a user would type, drug name first, 50 characters or fewer, at most 1 number, fully answered in the video. Vary the structure: at most 2 titles a week end in "What the Evidence Says" or "What the Trials Show". A run of identical title templates looks like mass-produced content.
- **Thumbnail:** "before-after" means a change of state: worried → answered, empty plate → protein plate, shedding → regrowth. **Never a body or weight before/after.** 4 words or fewer, never repeating the title, one labelled character, and the same hedge the video uses.
- **Publisher:** add every Lane A video to the "Life on Tirzepatide" playlist.

## Retention and linking
- The first spoken sentence answers the literal title. After that, open on a "you" scenario.
- Re-hook every 45–75 s. Name chapters after the questions people search.
- One subscribe ask, after the payoff. Keep this unchanged this week.
- End with: "There's a video I'd watch next, linked in the description." The publisher links the most closely related Lane A video. Never speak a title, and never say "on screen".
- **Publisher:** once the hair-loss long-form is verified live, add its link to line 1 of the description on both hair Shorts ("Will It Grow Back?" and "How Common Is It").

## Shorts (3 a day, 170 words or fewer, 60–85 s)
- **08:00, body-worry reassurance:** answer a fear people search for ("Will it…?", "Is it permanent?", "Is this normal?"). Give the honest answer, one new fact, and a line on when to see a doctor. Tirzepatide goes in the title. No hair Shorts this week.
- **13:00, lead.** Pick one:
  - a head-to-head with tirzepatide named first, in an obesity population (not diabetes-only);
  - new retatrutide Phase 3 data or a "what's confirmed?" fact, with a loop ending;
  - a fresh randomized result.

  Gray-market Shorts: at most 1 a week.
- **20:00, funnel (Exp D):** a fresh question that a live Lane A long-form answers. Targets this week: Hair Loss (once it's live), What to Eat, Side Effects, Protein. Last line: "Full breakdown on our channel, link in the description."
- **Exp F, 08:00 and 13:00 only:** the second-to-last spoken line is "We answer one tirzepatide question from the research every day. Subscribe if that helps." Then the usual last line. Don't add it to the 20:00 Short.
- **Banned:**
  - "Approved yet?" titles and "3 Ways" lists
  - brand-first titles, and semaglutide-only titles unless the evidence is semaglutide-only
  - cost Shorts and observational surgery angles
  - titles that name no drug, and scare framing
- **Variety:** any one trial in at most 1 Short a week, and a new fact in every piece.

## Quality gates (these protect the long-form slot)
- Before the mix, compare the speech-to-text transcript with the script for every number, every "point" and every drug name. Regenerate any scene that fails; don't ship it. Last week 3 of 9 long-forms were lost, including hair loss and stopping.
- Masking 0.02 or lower, measured last. Captions come from the on-screen text field.
- Every piece carries "Not personal advice" and the prescriber line. The fact-checker and the Editor-in-Chief always win.

## Carousels
- Make one only if the scheduler asks for it, and reuse verified Short text only.

## Experiments
- **Exp D (funnel):** the analyst logs the target long-form's viewCount and its SHORTS/RELATED traffic for 3 days before and 3 days after each 20:00 Short that had a verified link.
- **Exp E (thumbnail):** only the What to Eat thumbnail changes, to a state-change design (via Test & Compare, or a publisher swap from 11-04). Make no other edits to that video for 14 days.
- **Exp F (subscribe line):** the analyst logs subscribersGained per Short at day 7. Compare 08:00/13:00 Shorts (with the line) against 20:00 Shorts (without it), and channel subscribers per 1,000 YouTube views against the 3.6 baseline.
- **Hold constant:** 14:00 ET long-form slot, 8–12 min, retention rules, and the long-form subscribe ask.

experiments.name: Exp A: Practical tirzepatide long-forms (Lane A)
experiments.hypothesis: Long-tail practical tirzepatide questions that people search for beat approved-drug deep dives and keep gaining views over time.
experiments.change: Lane A on every day without qualifying news, with the long-tail searched question first in the title.
experiments.metric: Success: day-7 median of 25+ views and 60+ watch minutes, still growing at day 28.
experiments.result: Won at n=8+ (How Long, What to Eat, Side Effects, Strength, Plateau, Bones & Muscle, Protein, Thanksgiving). The 4 mature videos got 51, 115, 126 and 141 views (median about 120) and 204, 273, 412 and 433 min (median about 340), vs about 38 min for the 11 other GLP-1 long-forms. That's about 9× more. Suggested videos bring about 68% of Lane A minutes, at 5–6 min per view. Caveat: Plateau (12 views, 87 impressions at day 5) and Bones & Muscle (10 views, 67 impressions at day 4) start slowly but hold 68–79% of the video. Protein reached 146 views by day 3. Lane A is now the default for every 14:00 long-form.

experiments.name: Exp B: Gray-market 'what's actually confirmed' long-forms
experiments.hypothesis: Our strongest Short lane would also work as long-form.
experiments.change: 2 long-forms a week in lane B.
experiments.result: Closed early at n=1: the pharmacy check got 8 views and 20 min before it closed (11 views and 31 min now). Gray-market stays Shorts-only, at most 1 a week.

experiments.name: Exp C: First explainer within 48 h of a new named result
experiments.hypothesis: Being the first clear explainer of a newly public named trial result drives more long-form views than evergreen topics.
experiments.change: The long-form slot went to qualifying fresh randomized results.
experiments.result: Retired without reaching its sample. Only 1 valid video in the window: petrelintide, with 30 views and 97 min, below the 50-view bar. The only qualifying news this week (retatrutide vs semaglutide, 10-29) was dropped for audio. Looking back at fresh next-gen results (n=7): median about 35 views and about 97 min. Only EloraTZP was big. Lane A median is about 340 min, so the cost of giving the slot to news is too high. News now goes to 13:00 Shorts. Only a randomized head-to-head against tirzepatide or semaglutide may get an extra L2 long-form.

experiments.name: Exp D: Shorts-to-long-form funnel with a verified link
experiments.hypothesis: A 20:00 Short that asks a fresh question a live long-form answers, with a verified description link, lifts that long-form's daily views.
experiments.change: New targets: the 20:00 Short now points to live Lane A long-forms with the most minutes per view (Hair Loss once it's live, What to Eat, Side Effects, Protein) instead of EloraTZP. Last line and publisher link are unchanged.
experiments.metric: The target long-form's viewCount in the 3 days after the Short vs the 3 days before, plus its SHORTS and RELATED_VIDEO traffic. Success: an average lift of 10+ views a day, or 50%+ over the per-video baseline.
experiments.min_sample: n=6 funnel Shorts with a verified working link
experiments.result: No valid data point is logged yet. SHORTS traffic is still 0 on all 20 long-forms with traffic data. The analyst must log the target and link status for every 20:00 Short from 11-03.

experiments.name: Exp E: State-change thumbnail on What to Eat
experiments.hypothesis: What to Eat has a packaging problem, not a discovery problem: 1,290 impressions at 2.79% CTR. A state-change thumbnail of 4 words or fewer will lift CTR toward the 3.8–5.0% our similar thumbnails get.
experiments.change: Only the thumbnail changes: a state-change design of 4 words or fewer, no body imagery. Use the owner's Test & Compare if available; otherwise the publisher swaps it via the API on 11-04. Title and description stay as they are for 14 days.
experiments.metric: CTR on new impressions and views per day, vs 2.79% and the 7 days before the swap. Success: CTR of 3.5%+ with views per day not falling.
experiments.min_sample: 1,000 new impressions or 14 days, whichever comes later
experiments.result: Starts 11-04. Baseline: 1,290 impressions, 2.79% CTR, 115 views, 433 min. Strength (2.68% on 1,155) is next, but only after E reads out, so we change one variable at a time.

experiments.name: Exp F: A benefit-framed subscribe line in Shorts
experiments.hypothesis: Shorts bring about 300 YouTube views a day but almost no subscribers (about 0.5 per 1,000). One honest line that names the channel's promise will at least double conversion.
experiments.change: On 08:00 and 13:00 Shorts only, the second-to-last spoken line is: 'We answer one tirzepatide question from the research every day. Subscribe if that helps.' 20:00 Shorts get no line and act as the same-day control. Nothing else changes.
experiments.metric: subscribersGained per 1,000 views at day 7: 08:00/13:00 Shorts vs 20:00 Shorts. Also channel subscribers per 1,000 YouTube views vs the 10-27→11-02 baseline of about 3.6 (8 subscribers on about 2,250 views). Success: 2× the control rate and 2.5+ channel subscribers a day.
experiments.min_sample: 14 days (about 28 Shorts with the line, 14 without)
experiments.result: Starts 11-03. Subscriber counts per Short are small, so read the 14-day totals, not single Shorts.

owner_decisions: Build the cluster in Studio. Add end screens to all 10 practical tirzepatide videos (What to Eat, Strength, Side Effects, How Long, Plateau, Bones & Muscle, Protein, Thanksgiving, Food Noise, Constipation), pointing to 'best for viewer' plus the 'Life on Tirzepatide' playlist. Once the hair-loss long-form is live, set it as the related video on the 'Tirzepatide Hair Loss: Will It Grow Back?' Short (1,016 views) and pin a comment with its link; pinning can't be done through the API. Why: suggested videos bring about 68% of practical-video watch minutes at 5–6 min per view, playlist views run 8–12 min, and Shorts and end-screen traffic is 0 on all 20 long-forms we can measure. Expected effect: our first measurable Shorts→long-form traffic, and longer viewing chains inside the cluster. It takes about 30 minutes.

Run Test & Compare on What to Eat (1,290 impressions, 2.79% CTR), then on Strength (1,155, 2.68%), using a state-change thumbnail of 4 words or fewer, never a body before/after. Why: these two get the most impressions on the channel but click below the 3.8–5.0% our state-change thumbnails get at similar volume. Expected effect: about 35% more clicks on our two most-shown videos. If you can't do it by 11-04, the publisher will swap the What to Eat thumbnail through the API instead (Exp E).

Change the pipeline so audio-only drops get fixed instead of thrown away. When the Editor-in-Chief drops a long-form only for audio or subtitles (facts passed), regenerate the flagged scenes and re-run QA the same day. Give a fact-checker REVISE one automatic rewrite before marking the video failed. Why: 3 of 9 long-forms didn't ship from 10-27 to 11-01. Two were our highest-value topics (stopping tirzepatide, dropped for silent numbers, and hair loss, failed on REVISE even though the reviewer called the science 'solid'). The third was the only qualifying news head-to-head that week, lost to a 'rheumatoid' mispronunciation. Expected effect: about 2 more practical long-forms shipped a week. Each mature one earns about 340 min (about 5.7 h) in its first 2–3 weeks and keeps growing.

Change the cadence in config/channel.json. Set carouselDays to [] (about 50 carousels reached 0–4 people each). Add a second long-form slot on Mon/Wed/Fri for practical tirzepatide topics: either 10:00 ET with spacing.long lowered from 8 to 4 h (the 8 h rule blocks 10:00 next to 14:00), or 06:00 ET with spacing unchanged. Why: practical videos earn about 9× the watch minutes of other long-forms, and each new one feeds the suggested-video cluster that brings 68% of their minutes. Expected effect: +3 practical long-forms a week, about 17 extra watch hours per weekly batch once they mature, compounding toward the about 33 h a day YPP by Feb needs.
